name: University of Southern Denmark
about: SDU is spread across seven towns in the south and west of Denmark, and where you study matters more here than at any other Danish university. Its headquarters and most of its Danish-taught teaching are in Odense, but almost every fully English-taught bachelor's degree sits in Sønderborg, a small town on the island of Als by the German border, or in Vejle, SDU's newest campus and an IT-focused one. SDU is also unusual in how it admits people: an aptitude test called uniTEST is used for quota 2 on nearly all programmes, and SDU openly recommends that everyone sit it, including applicants whose grades would be good enough for quota 1.
ibNotes: A full IB Diploma qualifies you for admission to SDU's bachelor's programmes and bachelor of engineering programmes.

IB Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results or an IB Certificate qualify for a bachelor's programme only if you passed all six subjects with a minimum grade of 3, have at least three subjects at Higher Level, and have supplemented with at least two individual subjects (at least one at A level and one at B level). For a Bachelor of Engineering programme the supplementary subjects are not required.

SDU's IB results-service institution code is 000157. SDU states: "Without access to your online IB results, SDU cannot retrieve your IB documentation for admission." Tell your IB coordinator before you sit the exams.

SDU publishes its own IB conversion table. Mathematics A is met by IB Mathematics HL, Applications and Interpretation HL or Analysis and Approaches HL; Mathematics B by the SL versions. English A is met by English A1/A2, English A Literature, English A Language and Literature (SL or HL) or English B HL; English B is met by English B SL. Physics B is met by IB Physics SL. History B is met by IB History SL. Business-related requirements are met by Economics SL or Business and Management SL.

You can ask for a pre-assessment of your qualifications between 1 October and 15 November in the year before you apply — a useful safety net if you are unsure whether your subject choices clear the levels.
quotaNotes: SDU runs the usual Danish quota 1 and quota 2 split, but quota 2 at SDU is almost entirely an aptitude test called uniTEST. Quota 1 is decided on converted grade point average, and unusually SDU also sets a published minimum GPA to be considered in quota 1 at all: 7.0 on most BSc programmes, 6.0 on Economics and Business Administration in Sønderborg, and 5.0 on the three Bachelor of Engineering (BEng) programmes. Fall below it and your application can only be assessed in quota 2. Quota 2 places go to the applicants with the highest uniTEST scores. SDU says in its own words: "We recommend that everyone apply through quota 2 at SDU, even those with a grade point average sufficient to apply through quota 1." EU/EEA applicants whose grades convert are assessed on GPA unless they also sit the test; all non-EU/EEA applicants are invited to uniTEST because their grades are not converted. uniTEST is not a subject exam — it tests critical, quantitative and linguistic thinking, and all the information needed is given in the test.

deadlines.label: Pre-assessment of qualifications (optional)
deadlines.notes: Open from 1 October to 15 November in the year before you apply. SDU tells you whether your subjects and levels would qualify.

deadlines.label: Application (all applicants with a foreign exam, including IB)
deadlines.notes: SDU: "The application deadline for students with foreign degrees is March 15 at 12 noon." The portal optagelse.dk opens on 1 February.

deadlines.label: uniTEST registration
deadlines.notes: You register for the admission test after you have applied. Registration closes five days after the application deadline.

deadlines.label: uniTEST — in person at SDU Odense
deadlines.notes: SDU has already published the 2027 dates: 17 and 18 April 2027, written and paper-based, at Campusvej 55, 5230 Odense M. If you are in Denmark on the test date you must attend in person.

deadlines.label: uniTEST — online
deadlines.notes: 20–25 April 2027, taken online on your own computer with a live supervisor, if you are not in Denmark on the test dates. Your computer and room must meet technical requirements.

deadlines.label: Deadline to accept a study place

tuitionNonEu: Set per programme and paid a full year in advance: EUR 17,300 per year for the engineering and IT programmes (Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Electronics, Engineering Innovation and Business, Interactive Technology Engineering, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Software Engineering, and the three BEng programmes) and EUR 15,000 per year for European Studies, Economics and Business Administration (Sønderborg) and Market and Management Anthropology. Application fee EUR 200 per applicant regardless of how many programmes you apply for. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.

sources.title: SDU – Admission with an International Baccalaureate (IB)

notes: Campus is the single biggest decision at SDU, because the towns are genuinely far apart and nothing like each other.

Sønderborg holds eleven of SDU's fifteen fully English-taught bachelor's degrees. It is a small town on the island of Als in the far south of Jutland, closer to Flensburg in Germany than to any large Danish city, and several hours from Copenhagen by train. The campus, Alsion, is a single modern building shared with a concert hall, and the student body there is strongly international — partly because Danish applicants mostly do not move that far south. Mads Clausen's company Danfoss is based next door, which is why so much of the engineering sits here.

Vejle is SDU's newest campus and holds four English-taught degrees, all of them IT. SDU calls it "Denmark's newest IT campus". Vejle is a mid-sized town on the east coast of Jutland on the main motorway and rail line, with a cluster of IT employers nearby, so student jobs are realistic.

Odense is SDU's headquarters and Denmark's third-largest city, half an hour from Copenhagen by fast train — but only one fully English-taught bachelor's degree is taught there, Market and Management Anthropology. If you want Odense and you do not speak Danish, your options are almost nil at bachelor level.

SDU also has campuses in Kolding, Esbjerg, Slagelse and Copenhagen. None of them currently offers a fully English-taught bachelor's degree, so they are not options for an IB student who does not read Danish.

Robot Systems (Robotteknologi) in Odense is often assumed to be English-taught. It is not: SDU lists its tuition language as Danish. Robotics in English at SDU means Mechatronics in Sønderborg at bachelor level.

International Business Administration, Language and Culture (Sønderborg and EUF Flensborg) is listed among SDU's international programmes but is excluded here: SDU gives its tuition language as "English, German and Danish" and it requires Danish level A plus German at A or B level. It took only 6 students in 2026.

"All qualified applicants accepted" appears against most of the Sønderborg and Vejle programmes for 2026. That does not remove the entry requirements or the quota 1 GPA floor — it means everyone who met them and applied on time was offered a place.

The gap between expected places and the number actually admitted runs both ways. Mechatronics BSc expected 100 places and admitted 98; Software Engineering in Sønderborg expected 120 and admitted 44; Artificial Intelligence in Vejle expected 30 and admitted 66. Treat the place counts as planning figures, not caps.
A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. SDU repeats this on every programme page: "A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level."
SDU's own student total was not published in a form that could be verified on the pages checked, so it is left blank here rather than guessed.

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence
programmes.summary: A degree built specifically around machine learning, optimisation, logic and the ethics of automated decisions, rather than computer science with an AI module bolted on. SDU is explicit that you do not need to program before you start, but you do need to be comfortable with logical and mathematical thinking. Compared with the Computer Science degree on the same campus, it covers fewer classic computer science topics and goes deeper into AI.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor: "To be considered for a study place in quota 1, your GPA must be equivalent to 7.0 or higher in the Danish grading scale."
uniTEST is the quota 2 route and SDU recommends taking it even if you clear the quota 1 floor.
80 per cent of places in quota 1, 20 per cent in quota 2. 30 expected places; 66 admitted in 2026.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.summary: The broad computer science degree at SDU's IT campus: algorithms, software, databases, IT security and systems, with room to specialise later. Graduates go into software development, IT security, databases and game development, and many continue to a master's. Being next to a cluster of IT companies makes a relevant student job realistic during the degree.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
88 students admitted in 2026. SDU did not publish an expected number of study places for this programme on the page checked.

programmes.name: Software Engineering
programmes.summary: Software engineering as a craft: working out what users actually need, then designing, programming, testing and shipping software that survives contact with them. It includes how artificial intelligence and data are used inside ordinary systems. No prior programming is expected — there is an introductory course from the start.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale — this still applies even in a year when everyone qualified was admitted.
30 expected places; 47 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Interactive Technology Engineering
programmes.summary: Engineering aimed at the point where people meet machines: apps, interfaces, games, AI systems and interactive installations. You do the programming and the engineering, but you also do user research and design, so it suits someone who does not want to choose between the two. It is one of the few engineering degrees where a portfolio instinct is genuinely useful.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
30 expected places; 18 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Software Engineering
programmes.summary: The Sønderborg version of software engineering, with more weight on distributed systems, embedded devices, software architecture and cyber security — software that runs inside machines as much as on screens. Teaching is in international project groups. No prior programming experience is expected.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
120 expected places; 44 admitted in 2026.

programmes.name: Mechatronics
programmes.summary: Mechanics, electronics and software taught as one subject, because that is how robots, automated production lines and medical devices are actually built. You get a broad toolbox — mechanics, electronics, programming, power electronics, thermodynamics, data-driven methods — and spend a lot of time on problems brought in from industry. This is SDU's largest English-taught engineering intake.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
100 expected places; 47 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.summary: Classical mechanical engineering — mechanics, materials, structural design, simulation and product development — with a steady push towards sustainable design and modern manufacturing. You spend real time on 3D modelling, calculation and testing, and on communicating technical decisions to people who are not engineers. It has the widest set of alternative science entry routes of any SDU English-taught degree.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. And one of: Physics level B and Chemistry level C; Physics level B and Biotechnology level A; Geoscience level A and Chemistry level C.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
65 expected places; 50 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Electronics
programmes.summary: Designing, building and testing electronic systems: analogue and digital electronics, programming, signal processing and control engineering, resting on a heavy foundation of mathematics and physics. You work with electric motors, sensors, power electronics and intelligent control, and with both the hardware and the software side. A small intake in a town built around electronics manufacturing.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
30 expected places; 24 admitted in 2026.

programmes.name: Engineering, Innovation and Business
programmes.summary: An engineering degree for the person who wants to stand between the developers and the market. You get the technical base — mechanics, electronics, programming, industrial simulation and process tools — alongside business development, entrepreneurship and innovation management, so you can judge whether a technical idea is worth building. The entry requirements are the same as for the pure engineering degrees; the content is not.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
65 expected places; 58 admitted in 2026.

programmes.name: Mechatronics
programmes.summary: The applied version of Mechatronics: the same mix of mechanics, electronics and software, but organised around industrial practice and ending in a six-month internship, so that you are employable as an engineer after three and a half years. You can still continue to a master's afterwards. The quota 1 grade floor is markedly lower than on the BSc.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor: "To be considered for a study place in quota 1, your GPA must be equivalent to 5.0 or higher in the Danish grading scale."
40 expected places; 98 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.summary: A practice-first mechanical engineering degree, with company projects from early on and a six-month internship built into the final year. It is aimed at going straight into industry after three and a half years rather than at a research career, though a master's remains open. It offers the broadest set of alternative science entry combinations at SDU.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. And one of: Physics level B and Chemistry level C; Physics level B and Biotechnology level A; Geoscience level A and Chemistry level C; Geoscience level A and Biotechnology level A.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 5.0 on the Danish scale.
65 expected places; 85 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Electronics
programmes.summary: Hands-on electronics engineering: analogue and digital circuits, signal processing, high-frequency technology and electric motors, with semester projects such as smart homes, motor testing and drone control. Mathematics is heavy in the first part. The sixth semester is a six-month internship in Denmark or abroad.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level A. Physics level B or Geoscience level A. Course levels refer to the Danish high school system: A is advanced, B is intermediate, and C is beginner level.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 5.0 on the Danish scale.
40 expected places; 32 admitted in 2026 (national admissions list).

programmes.name: Economics and Business Administration
programmes.summary: A broad business economics degree with everything framed around companies that trade across borders — fitting, given that the campus sits on the German border. Your year group will be Danish and other European students, taught entirely in English. It has the lowest quota 1 grade floor of SDU's non-engineering English-taught degrees.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level B. History level B or Social Sciences level B or History of Ideas level B or Contemporary History level B or International Economy level B.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor: from 2027 your GPA must be equivalent to 7.0 or higher on the Danish scale to be considered in quota 1 (it was 6.0 until 2026).
65 expected places; 103 admitted in 2026.
SDU prints the third requirement as "International Economy level B"; this is the Danish subject International Economics (International Økonomi).

programmes.name: European Studies
programmes.summary: An interdisciplinary social science degree about how European regions, institutions and cross-border co-operation actually work, taught in small classes on the Danish-German border — which is the live case study. You learn to design and run development projects with a regional, national or European focus and to explain the results to decision-makers.
programmes.requirementsText: To be eligible for admission, you must hold a qualifying upper secondary school degree, and you must have passed the following courses: English level B. Mathematics level B. History level B or Social Sciences level B or History of Ideas level B or Contemporary History level B.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
45 expected places; 76 admitted in 2026.

programmes.name: Market and Management Anthropology
programmes.summary: Anthropology used as a business tool: fieldwork, cross-cultural analysis and the study of how people actually behave as consumers, combined with management. It includes a compulsory period of fieldwork abroad in a country you choose. SDU runs it as a "signature programme" — a small intake with intense teaching and frequent feedback — and it is the only fully English-taught bachelor's degree on the Odense campus.
programmes.requirementsText: In addition you must have passed: English level B. Mathematics level B. History level B or Social Sciences level B or History of Ideas level B or Contemporary History level B.
extraRequirements: Quota 1 GPA floor of 7.0 on the Danish scale.
Compulsory fieldwork abroad in a country of your choice.
40 expected places; 48 admitted in 2026. It has the highest 2026 cut-off of any SDU English-taught bachelor's degree.
